key_insight: The paper introduces an efficient classical simulation framework for hybrid CV-DV quantum circuits by representing the continuous-variable part as a linear combination of Gaussian functions while keeping the discrete-variable part in blocks.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable analysis of mixed quantum hardware and algorithms without Fock-space truncation, which is important for designing and validating hybrid photonic and cavity-QED systems.
method: Decompose the hybrid density matrix into DV basis blocks and expand each CV block as a linear combination of Gaussians (LCoG).
Apply Gaussian operations analytically to each Gaussian term independently, including controlled Gaussian operations.
Extend the framework to controlled Gaussian channels with state-dependent Gaussian noise.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an example simulation of Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) state generation in a cavity-QED system, demonstrating the method on a hybrid quantum protocol.
watch_item: The approach is efficient per Gaussian term, but practical performance may still depend on the number of Gaussian components needed for accurate representation of the state.
paper_title: Efficient Simulation of Hybrid Continuous- and Discrete-Variable Quantum Circuits via Gaussian Decompositions
